incident-bot: PAGER: abnormal surge in fncall/agent-invoke errors across us-west-2, triggered at 2026-03-15T09:22:12Z. Error rate: 14x baseline, 72% of requests touching tool-invoke path. Paging oncall rota: Ava

Ava (oncall): seeing repeated 5xx from invoke-proxy, spike correlated with structured-output streaming requests. Dash: https://redwood.internal/d/alerts/fncall-surge

Ravi (sre): confirmed. KPs: invoke-5xx, invoke-queue-latency, and a rising number of model OOM retries. Looks like a bad traffic pattern from a handful of tenants plus a general flood from free-tier streaming.

Taylor (eng): probable root: a recent prompt template that makes agents call many small tools per turn. Combined with streaming+structured-output we get lots of KV cache churn -> memory thrash -> model restarts.

Ava (oncall): immediate mitigation options:
- temporary global throttle on agent/toolcalls
- per-tenant rate caps for tool invocation
- disable structured JSON streaming on free/trial tiers
- fallback to plain text responses for streaming requests

Jordan (support): we already have 3 customer threads from acme-corp and novaai complaining about timeouts. They are on paid tiers but with burst policies. Need targeted mitigation so paid customers keep service.

Taylor (eng): propose selective approach:
1) Enable per-plan invoke gating: paid-enterprise -> full; paid-standard -> soft-limit; free/trial -> deny fncall and structured-output streaming.
2) Deploy a quick feature-flag to the API gateway that drops toolcall field on incoming requests for free/trial tenants (syntactic scrub).
3) Apply temporary token-level throttle for invoke API: 20 invoke/sec global, 5 invoke/sec free per-tenant.

Ava (oncall): can we do that without a rollback? Need to avoid config-heavy deploys. Ravi/Taylor, who can flip flags?

Taylor (eng): I can push a gateway-only flag, no model changes. Will do a staged rollout: runbook below.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by Taylor for feature-flag: "ff/deny-free-toolcalls" to env=prod-us-west-2. CI: green. ETA 2m.

Taylor (eng): runbook:
- step 0: enable read-only mode for structured streaming on free tenants via gateway header rewrite.
- step 1: enable per-tenant invoke caps in traffic-shaper (rbac key: traffic-shaper.write).
- step 2: monitor metrics: invoke-5xx, stream-drop-rate, model-ooms.
- step 3: revert if paid-customer impact > 1% or errors persist.

Ravi (sre): applying traffic-shaper caps now: commands:
```
# restrict invoke for free tier
traffic-shaper set-cap --plan free --invoke-rps 5 --scope us-west-2
# global soft cap
traffic-shaper set-cap --global --invoke-rps 20
```

Ava (oncall): Jordan, please prepare customer comms for acme-corp & novaai. We will exempt enterprise-paid tenants from this change.

Jordan (support): drafting now. Short note: "We are applying temporary measures to reduce tool-invocations for trial and free accounts to stabilize latency. Paid accounts unaffected. Investigating root cause." Will post once Taylor confirms the flag is live.

Taylor (eng): flipping ff/deny-free-toolcalls -> ON for us-west-2. Command: `kubectl set env deploy/gateway FF_DENY_FREE_TOOLCALLS=true -n api-proxy-usw2`

deploy-bot: feature flag enabled in prod-us-west-2 by Taylor.

Ava (oncall): starting 10m quiet window to monitor. Metrics: invoke-5xx dropping, queue-length down 30%, model OOMs reduced from 18/min to 4/min.

Ravi (sre): good signal. Now applying structured-output streaming downgrade for free tier: gateway will return content-type: text/plain and strip `tool_call` blocks. Patching proxy rule: `proxy-rewrite strip_toolcalls_free`

Taylor (eng): adding fallback behavior in router: if request plan==free and contains tools -> respond with streaming plain text with a short CTA about upgrading. Snippet we return to users:
```
{"warning":"Tool calls temporarily disabled for this session. Upgrade to a paid plan for full tool access."}
```

Ava (oncall): Jordan send comms now, mention ACME and NOVA are exempt if they are paid.

Jordan (support): sent messages to affected customers and internal CSMs. Template used: "We're applying a short stabilization change that limits agent/tool invocations on free trials. This should reduce latency and prevent errors; paid customers are unaffected. We'll follow up when fully resolved."

Ravi (sre): monitoring window update: 25m after toggles - overall errors down 72%, p95 latency improved by 200ms. No paid-customer incidents reported. Free-tier dropped 90% tool calls as expected.

Ava (oncall): good. Next steps:
- Taylor to roll permanent mitigations: quota smoothing, prefix caching for agents, and model kernel tunings.
- Ravi to run a post-mortem with traffic fingerprinting to identify offending prompt templates and tenants.
- Jordan to list customers contacted and any follow-ups.

Taylor (eng): logging follow-up PRs:
- PR #5421: traffic-shaper per-plan policies (long-term)
- PR #5422: gateway rewrite rules for structured streaming fallback
- PR #5423: add telemetry to detect high-tool-call-rate prompts and auto-suggest quantization/profile

Ava (oncall): handoff to Ravi for L2. If anything regresses, page me immediately. Marking incident as mitigation-in-progress.

Ravi (sre): taking ownership for post-mortem. Paging pattern: escalate to eng-runtime if we see >10% residual 5xx after 2h.

Taylor (eng): FYI snippets of logs that helped root cause:
```
2026-03-15T09:18:37Z gateway: req_id=abc123 plan=free stream=true tools_count=12 tokens=2400
runtime: alloc_failed: kvcache evict spike -> model_restarts
```

Jordan (support): added support tickets: RED-10234 (ACME), RED-10235 (NOVA). Noted that both are paid and were exempt; checked their metrics - no impact.

Ava (oncall): closing the active paging loop. We will leave flags on for the next 4 hours and re-evaluate in the postmortem. Thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated: toolcall-induced OOMs reduced. Actions: flags applied, per-plan caps, customer comms sent. Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 at 2026-03-15T10:04:12Z."
